fields.notes: Wishbone B4 is a wire-level / cycle-level bus protocol specification. It defines only logical signal semantics and timing rules relative to [CLK_I] (Chapter 6 — Tpd,clk-su = 1/Fclk constraint per signal path). It explicitly does NOT define PDK-specific SDC, floorplan / placement constraints, clock-tree budgets, or IO standards (1.2 Objectives — independent of hardware technology, independent of synthesis tool / router / layout tool technology, independent of logic signaling levels, independent of FPGA/ASIC test methodologies). Per-implementation timing closure is the responsibility of the SoC integrator and is captured outside this protocol spec.
fields.spec_provided_timing_constraint: Chapter 6 defines exactly one timing parameter: Tpd,clk-su = 1/Fclk (clock-to-setup propagation delay) per signal path. Maximum clock frequency Fclk is dictated by the time delay between a positive [CLK_I] edge and the setup on a stage further down the logical signal path. RULE 5.00 — all WISHBONE output signals registered at rising [CLK_I], all WISHBONE input signals stable before rising [CLK_I]. RULE 5.05 — synchronous, RTL design methodologies. OBSERVATION 5.10 — WISHBONE assumes a low-skew clock distribution scheme.
implementation_recommendations: RECOMMENDATION 3.15 — design WISHBONE MASTER interfaces so that there are no intermediate logic gates between a registered flip-flop and the signal outputs on [STB_O] and [CYC_O] (delay timing on these signals are very often the most critical paths).
OBSERVATION 3.15 — if a gated clock generator is used, and if the clock is stopped, then the WISHBONE interface is not capable of responding to its [RST_I] signal.

OBSERVATION 3.50 — registered [ACK_O] / [ERR_O] / [RTY_O] significantly reduces the loopback delay in large high-speed designs at the cost of one additional wait state per transfer (or zero wait state if Registered Feedback bus cycles are used).
PERMISSION 5.00 — the user's place and route tool MAY be used to enforce RULE 5.00.

evidence.quote: The WISHBONE specification is designed to provide the end user with very simple timing constraints. Although the application specific circuit(s) will vary in this regard, the interface itself is designed to work without the need for detailed timing specifications. The clock input [CLK_I] to each IP core MUST coordinate all activities for the internal logic within the WISHBONE interface. All WISHBONE output signals MUST be registered at the rising edge of [CLK_I]. All WISHBONE input signals MUST be stable before the rising edge of [CLK_I]. The user's place and route tool MAY be used to enforce RULE 5.00.

Independent of hardware technology (FPGA, ASIC, etc.). Independent of delivery method (soft, firm or hard core). Independent of synthesis tool, router and layout tool technology. Independent of FPGA and ASIC test methodologies. Independent of logic signaling levels.
